podcast.title: Substitute for Robert Johnson (1938)
podcast.body: Big Bill Broonzy was recruited to perform at the 1938 "Spirituals to Swing" concerts after its organizer, John Hammond, discovered that Robert Johnson had recently died. Broonzy also played a couple of Johnson's records from the stage. "They'd got Big Bill Bruinsy to play in his place, and played a couple of Johnson's records from the stage."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Appearance on 6-5 Special
podcast.body: He made an appearance on the BBC's television program "6-5 Special," which was considered one of the show's exceptional moments. "By all accounts it had some fantastic moments, including an appearance by Big Bill Vunze and a live broadcast from the two eyes coffee bar itself."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 70: "Move It" by Cliff Richard and the Drifters

podcast.title: Second Career as Folk Blues Musician
podcast.body: His performance at "Spirituals to Swing" jump-started Broonzy's later career as a folk blues musician, where he primarily played for white audiences, a shift from his earlier role as a Chicago blues performer for black audiences. "That had in fact kick-started Bruinsy's later second career as a folk blues musician, playing for largely white audiences, rather than as a photo Chicago blues performer, playing for blackwings."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 97: "Song to Woody" by Bob Dylan

podcast.title: Skiffle Repertoire
podcast.body: His songs were a primary component of the repertoire for skiffle groups, alongside those of Lead Belly and Woody Guthrie. He was notable as the one blues musician that even the least knowledgeable skifflers could name, despite his relatively limited commercial success in the US. "a repertoire that was made up primarily of songs by Lead Belly, Woody Guthrie and Big Bill Brunze, who was the one blues musician that even the least knowledgeable Skiffle could name, despite his relative lack of commercial success in the US."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 70: "Move It" by Cliff Richard and the Drifters

podcast.title: Spirituals to Swing Appearance
podcast.body: He was a then-obscure folk musician who replaced a deceased Johnson (unrelated to Pete Johnson) in the lineup for John Hammond's "Spirituals to Swing" concert in 1938. His appearance at this pivotal concert significantly contributed to his rise in popularity. "Johnson's place was taken by a then obscure folk musician called Big Bill Roonsy, who became popular largely on the basis of that appearance."
